draft_evidence.quote: He knew three things about it that were not guesses, and he counted them. It had been there before Oryn; session nine was five years old and she was two months. It had been there before Brom's read caught it, because a read catches what is already there. And it was not the Quiet — the Quiet was outside him, a line on the ground that stopped Paths, and this was inside, and the fragments went round it, and had for longer than he had owned any.

comparison_evidence.quote: Cael's first self-reading, described ONLY as location and sensation (a place at the center that the nine — ten — go around; not a fragment; earlier than any Tide source) — no name, no theory, no 'still place' phrase yet (Ch22 names it), no 'primordial/before/source'.

findings.consequence: Grammatically, 'the fragments' remains the subject of 'had [gone round it]', so the sentence says acquired fragments were already circling the anomaly before Cael owned any fragment. That contradicts the acquisition ledger. If the intended subject is instead the anomaly, the clause is unclear and still asserts that it predates every fragment, an ontological chronology the packet does not authorize. The line therefore replaces the removed design implication with a different reader-facing lore claim.
findings.repair_target: Keep the verified removal of design/purpose language, but constrain the temporal comparison to established facts: location and movement; before Oryn; before Brom's read caught it; earlier than any Tide source. Do not imply fragment action before acquisition or that the anomaly predates all fragments.
